Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2544); Emmor (i.e. Chamor), a Canaanite:--Emmor.
BiblicalUsage: Emmor is the Greek form of Hamor, the Canaanite whose sons sold Abraham the burial ground at Sychem. Stephen names him once, in Acts 7:16, when the patriarchs were carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought from the sons of Emmor. His life story is told under Hamor.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even a single name in Stephen's speech matters — Abraham's purchase was real land bought from real men, and God's promises have always been anchored in real ground. Emmor's part is small, but it is part of the deed.
